text:
Marathon Petroleum stock has climbed nearly 10% over the past two weeks, with today's modest gain of 0.69% continuing that uptrend. The core driver is geopolitical tension in the Middle East—Iran has closed the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure have intensified, and flames were reported near Riyadh's airport on September 19th. These disruptions to global oil supplies have pushed world crude prices to $130.80 per barrel, a level high enough to improve refining margins and boost the value of Marathon's operations.

US refineries are running at 96.8% capacity with strong demand signals, and inventory levels remain moderate—conditions that typically favor margin-friendly operations when crude prices spike due to supply concerns. The market appears to be pricing in sustained elevated oil costs from the Middle East tensions rather than expecting a quick resolution, which benefits refiners that can process crude into fuel and sell it at elevated prices.
